record.notes: Approved by the Council of Ministers on 4 December 2025 and published in Diário da República n.º 5/2026, Série I, on 8 January 2026; in force from the following day. The agenda carries out Initiative 10 of the National Digital Strategy (Resolution of the Council of Ministers 207/2024) and rests on six guiding principles, the first being responsible innovation. The action plan for 2026-2030 may be updated by the government member responsible for State reform together with the member responsible for finance; commitments depend on available funding, mainly European funds, and the Council for Digital in Public Administration monitors implementation. The plan also includes a national AI literacy campaign on risks and responsible use (initiative III.8, first half of 2026) and a programme encouraging voluntary certification of AI quality management under Portuguese Standard 4595 (initiative IV.2).
record.scope_note: Mainly an agenda for AI infrastructure, adoption, talent and productivity; included as Portugal's national AI agenda, whose Responsibility and Ethics axis plans the AI Act's implementation, regulatory sandboxes and national risk-assessment tools.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the Diário da República page of the resolution rendered in a browser (diariodarepublica.pt), which gives the issuer, the publication in Diário da República n.º 5/2026, Série I, of 2026-01-08, the status 'Em vigor', the operative paragraphs 1 to 6, the signature of 4 December 2025 and annexes I and II with initiatives IV.1 to IV.7; and the PDF of the same issue (files.diariodarepublica.pt, stored as the record's secondary source). The plain download of the page has no text, and the browser's print copy holds only OCR of the page frame. Version 1's notes on ANACOM (the announced AI Act designation, the Commission's list of 7 September 2026, the Article 77 list, the consultation on the Article 5 prohibitions and two later resolutions) rest on pages not stored in this run and were removed; they are listed as leads. No English version was found: the Government's digital.gov.pt page on the agenda (not stored) says the document is available in Portuguese only.
